values: The permit effective date and its relationship to the Federal FY2025 evaluation window (2024-10-01 through 2025-09-30)
Whether footnote *9 is scoped solely to the WET monitoring row that references it or governs commencement of other Part I monitoring and reporting requirements shown on adjacent pages
PART II Whole Effluent Toxicity testing requirements referenced by footnote *9 for additional WET monitoring conditions and frequency reduction option

grounding.excerpt: *9      Monitoring and reporting requirements begin on the effective date of this permit. See PART II, Whole Effluent Toxicity testing requirements for additional WET monitoring and reporting conditions, and a frequency reduction option.

WHOLE EFFLUENT TOXICITY TESTING ... (*9) ... Footnotes: ... *9 Monitoring and reporting requirements begin on the effective date of this permit. ... *10 The limits begin on the effective date of this permit ...

payload.rationale: The obligation chains three judgments: commencement on the permit effective date, scope of footnote *9 (WET row only vs broader Part I monitoring), and whether any Federal FY2025 period before that effective date lies outside applicable obligations. Footnote *9 explicitly states that monitoring and reporting requirements begin on the permit effective date, which is affirmative commencement language, but the packet does not establish the permit effective date, so the relationship to the FY2025 window (2024-10-01 through 2025-09-30) cannot be grounded. Scope is likewise unsettled: *9 is cited only on the Whole Effluent Toxicity row, yet its wording is general ('Monitoring and reporting requirements'), while adjacent Part I pollutant rows use separate footnotes (*1, *2, *10, etc.) without referencing *9—neither narrow WET-only scope nor broad Part I governance is established. PART II WET requirements are referenced but not included in the packet, leaving the third value unassessed. ACCEPT would require grounded evidence for the full chained proposition; REJECT would require establishing that the proposition cannot hold, which the commencement text and missing effective date do not support. Per P5, neither burden is met; UNRESOLVED is the correct disposition.
